Subject: Re: Demo: inference commitments & mutual action items (latency/streaming)

Thanks for the demo today — the team appreciated the streaming examples and the ability to fall back to a lower-cost variant. A few things we need to confirm as we evaluate: 

1) Latency targets: for our live product we need 95th percentile generation latency <= 250ms for short prompts (~64 tokens). Is that achievable with your hosted offering or would we need Dedicated?

2) Throughput/concurrency: expected steady-state concurrency is ~200 QPS during business hours, burst to 1k QPS for peak. Do you recommend autoscaling on Dedicated or a mix of Hosted + Dedicated fallback?

3) Streaming tolerance: we use token streaming to render partial responses. Any known upper bound on connection concurrency (websocket/stream connections) and recommended socket timeouts?

We can share sample traces and a small corpus for a quick benchmark. Can you send a short mutual action plan (MAP) with acceptance criteria so our infra team can sign off?

Thanks,
Amit
Product Lead, Neurolytics

Hi Amit / Priya — great to meet you both on the call. Short answer up front: yes, we can meet aggressive P95 latency with the right configuration; whether that requires Dedicated depends on your tolerance for tail variability and cost. Below is a concise MAP and proposed next steps we can convert to a shared doc. I included Ben (sales) for procurement cadence, Karthik (solutions) for the bench planning, and Soojin (CS) to own runbook and observability.

Mutual Action Plan (high level) — proposed
- Stage 0 (Discovery / baseline) — Neurolytics provides 2k sample requests and 1-minute traces representative of short prompts. Redwood runs a 1-hour perf bench on Hosted and returns P50/P95/P99 latency and token cost. Deliverable: baseline report. Target date: 2028-03-12.
- Stage 1 (Pilot / canary) — 2-week pilot on Dedicated (reserved small pool) with traffic mirror at 5% production. Acceptance criteria: P95 <= 250ms for 64-token prompts, tail no worse than 2x baseline, stream framing < 80ms first-token-to-first-byte for 90% connections. Deliverable: pilot report + runbook. Target start: 2028-03-20.
- Stage 2 (Rollout) — capacity plan for steady 200 QPS, autoscale thresholds, and fallback path to Hosted. Deliverable: capacity runbook + cost estimate. Target: 2028-04-05.

Quick clarifications we need from you to lock MAP:
- Exact token distribution for the short prompts (median, 90th).
- Typical response length in tokens.
- Maximum acceptable failover latency (when falling back to Hosted or cheaper quantized model).

Attachments: I attached an SLO checklist and a template we use for the pilot runbook (redwood-slo-checklist.xlsx). We also recommend sharing your sample traces as network-trace-20280302.log.

Next internal steps for Redwood team (Ben / Karthik / Soojin):
- Karthik: synth bench plan and config for both Hosted and Dedicated (due 2028-03-09).
- Soojin: draft pilot runbook and monitoring dashboard template (due 2028-03-11).
- Ben: propose commercial structure (pilot credits, committed monthly) and draft statement for procurement (due 2028-03-10).

Amit/Priya — if that looks right we’ll turn this into a shared Google doc and propose calendar slots for the bench next week.

Best,
Tessa Morgan

Thanks Tessa — MAP looks good. A couple of additions/questions from infra/security: 

- For the pilot we need a network egress estimate (GB/day) and an outline of how KV cache warmup is handled during a canary (cold vs warm cache behavior).
- Can you confirm whether the hosted fallback preserves PII controls (we need attestations about data separation for this evaluation)?
- We’ll also need an easy way to replay the 5% mirrored traffic for replay testing without impacting production.

We can share the sample traces tomorrow. For the token distribution: median 48 tokens, 90th 88 tokens, typical response 100–180 tokens. Peak bursts are driven by synchronous user-driven flows (spikes ~1k QPS for ~7 minutes).

If possible, please include proposed canary rollback criteria (when to abort) — e.g., sustained P95 degradation > 20% over baseline for 10 minutes or error rate > 2%.

—Amit

Amit — great details, thanks. We’ll incorporate everything into the MAP and add explicit canary rollback thresholds. Summary of updates we will add to the shared doc: 

Bench assumptions and deliverables
- Token distribution: median 48, 90th 88 (from your note).
- Test workloads: 1-hour baseline bench (hosted) + 1-hour dedicated bench + 1-hour mirrored 5% traffic replay.
- Egress estimate: we’ll provide a per-token GB estimate post-bench; preliminary ballpark for your profile is ~15–25 GB/day at steady 200 QPS with 120-token average output (we’ll refine after sample traces).
- KV cache warmup: we’ll run both cold-start runs and a warm-cache run; pilot runbook will include cache-warming guidance and a warmup script.

Canary rollback / abort criteria (proposed)
- Abort if sustained P95 > 20% above baseline for 10 consecutive minutes.
- Abort if error rate (5xx / user-visible errors) > 2% in any 5-minute window.
- Abort if first-byte streaming latency (TTFB) increases by > 100ms for > 15% of connections.

Deliverables and timeline (updated)
- 2028-03-09: Redwood bench plan and config (Karthik).
- 2028-03-11: Pilot runbook draft and monitoring dashboard (Soojin).
- 2028-03-12: Baseline report (Redwood).
- 2028-03-20: Pilot start (subject to procurement).

Action items for Neurolytics
- Share sample traces and corpus by 2028-03-08.
- Confirm procurement lead and PO cadence so Ben can propose pilot economics.

I’ll create the shared MAP doc now and invite your infra team. Attaching the SLO checklist and an example rollback snippet in the Drive folder.

Talk soon — we’ll circle back once Ben has procurement options.

Best regards,
